definitions.explanation: a traditional Japanese celebration held approximately 100 days after a baby's birth, featuring a symbolic first meal ceremony

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんの{百日|ももか}{祝|いわ}いをした。
{百日|ももか}{祝|いわ}いの{写真|しゃしん}をスタジオで{撮|と}った。
examples.english: We took photos for the 100-day celebration at a studio.

examples.japanese: {百日|ももか}{祝|いわ}いでは、{赤|あか}ちゃんが{一生|いっしょう}{食|た}べ{物|もの}に{困|こま}らないようにと{願|ねが}いを{込|こ}めてお{食|く}い{初|ぞ}めの{儀式|ぎしき}を{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: At the 100-day celebration, a symbolic first-meal ceremony is held with the wish that the baby will never lack food throughout life.

notes:
A milestone celebration for a baby at approximately 100 days old. The centerpiece is the お{食|く}い{初|ぞ}め ceremony, where a symbolic meal is set before the baby (who does not actually eat it) to wish for a lifetime of abundance.

THE お{食|く}い{初|ぞ}め CEREMONY:
- A tray of ceremonial foods is prepared, typically including {鯛|たい} (sea bream), {赤飯|せきはん} (red rice), {煮物|にもの} (simmered dish), {吸|す}い{物|もの} (clear soup), and {香|こう}の{物|もの} (pickles)
- {歯|は}{固|がた}めの{石|いし} — a small stone placed on the tray to wish for strong teeth
- The eldest family member pretends to feed the baby using chopsticks

ALTERNATIVE NAMES:
- お{食|く}い{初|ぞ}め — first-meal ceremony (the most commonly used name)
- {百日|ひゃくにち}の{祝|いわ}い — 100-day celebration (on'yomi reading)

RELATED CELEBRATIONS:
- お{七夜|しちや} — 7th-night naming ceremony
- お{宮参|みやまい}り — first shrine visit (around 30 days)
- {初節句|はつぜっく} — first seasonal festival
- {初|はつ}{誕生|たんじょう} — first birthday
